title: Старые знакомые и визит Игоря  (Old Acquaintances and Igor's Visit)

segments.t: In front of the whole kitchen, Valdemar Barani embraces Chef Barinov and announces that Viktor Petrovich was his very first chef and mentor in Paris. Meanwhile, Vika returns to her building only to find Igor waiting by her door, demanding to know why she ignores his text messages.
Слушай, вижу, у тебя все в порядке.
Ну, потому что мне тебе нечего ответить.
Ну, так бы и ответила, что нечего ответить.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'How many years has it been?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'how much' and finishing on 'years'. Vika answers right away.
Слушай, вижу, у тебя все в порядке.
'Listen, I see everything is going well for you.' Vika addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'order'.
'Back in the kitchen again?' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'again', while 'kitchen' completes the thought.
'I see the two of you know each other.' Vika chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'acquainted' to keep a polite distance. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Viktor Petrovich was my first head chef.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'Viktor', while 'chef' completes the thought.
'My teacher.' In Russian, the idea of 'my' flows naturally into 'teacher' without extra filler words.
'Where it is best to set up the equipment.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'where' before landing on 'equipment'. Vika answers right away.
'We will talk later.' The grammar packs 'later' and 'we'll have a talk' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Igor, what are you doing here?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Igor' before landing on 'are you doing'.
'You are not replying to my text messages.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'SMS'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Ну, потому что мне тебе нечего ответить.
'Well, because I have nothing to say to you.' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'answer' in spoken Russian.
Ну, так бы и ответила, что нечего ответить.
'Then you could have replied that you have nothing to say.' Vika anchors the line on 'come on', while 'answer' completes the thought.
'Are you waiting for someone?' Chef Viktor raises the pitch on 'are waiting' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Слушай, вижу, у тебя все в порядке.
Ну, потому что мне тебе нечего ответить.
Ну, так бы и ответила, что нечего ответить.

That wraps up this scene as barani warmly greets Viktor Petrovich as his first teacher while the Chef seethes, and outside Vika's apartment persistent admirer Igor confronts Vika for ignoring his messages. Until next time!
